name: stage2_region
description: Provenance-pinned capture_image_with_Bulb ARM code region (issue #18). The binary itself is proprietary Benro firmware, is never committed, and must be supplied locally (see stage2_region.bin.placeholder). This sidecar records only coordinates and hashes - no firmware content.

provenance.layout_note: entry_address and code_address are the RELOCATED load address used by the emulator, not the original ELF symbol address. The blob is written at code_address and execution starts at entry_address, so for a 2176-byte blob entry_address must equal code_address. symbol_vaddr records the true ELF address for provenance only. ARMEmulator now rejects (fail closed) any layout where entry_address falls outside the loaded bytes: such a run executes zero-filled pages and can report PASS without ever touching the artifact. The absolute symbol address 0x101aac is not page aligned, so it cannot be used as code_address directly; use a page-aligned base such as 0x1000 or 0x101000.
provenance.stub_entries_note: Deliberately empty. The region contains 42 BL/BLX sites whose targets lie outside the extracted window, so their semantic identities (camera/libgphoto/timer/callback) cannot be resolved from the region alone. Resolving them requires the source ELF's symbol table, which is not retained. Declaring addresses here without verified names would invent a boundary contract, which issue #15 forbids.

observed_behaviour.interpretation: ARM decoding is correct: the region's real instructions execute. The run then faults reading a pointer argument that was never initialised, because no caller frame or stub wiring exists yet. Full lifecycle execution needs AAPCS argument setup plus resolved stub entries.

source_retention_gap.detail: The pinned region does NOT match the same symbol/size extracted from the retained stock baseline pgphoto.stock (Benro 4.0.0.32), which hashes 333a3f669734459807c0dc601af6f9dad1d857a51acf546da1210bd5461f7f19 at the same entry 0x101aac and size 2176. The pinned blob is therefore a patched build, not stock. The v90-era source binary that produced it is not retained anywhere on this host; only the extracted region survives. Until the owning build is identified and retained, this region cannot be re-derived from a firmware zip or device pull.
